# Special contact observations

`special_contacts.tsv` records original SPIKEPOINT, OCHRE, and SILVER `touchEffects1` calls.
Two source runs and the bundled JAR produce identical bytes.
All four compiled helper classes also match across both backends.
The canonical corpus contains 355 cases, 711 snapshots, and 356 actual contact calls.

## Source and comparison contract

The source authority is the pinned supplied `Organism.java`.
SPIKEPOINT occupies lines `11281-12004`, OCHRE `12005-12194`, and SILVER `12195-12742`.
Each call includes the shared recipient-energy death guard at `13106-13108`.
The helper invokes the actual private `touchEffects1(Organism,int,int)` through reflection.
Before every call, it checks exact current attacker ARGB against its labelled branch.
It does not calculate expected damage, velocity, infection, death, statistics, or RNG results.

The fixed ledger and typed input inventory precede Rust replay.
Compare scalar, photo, gas, statistics, velocity, endpoint, color, reaction, identity, and RNG observations exactly.
Preserve signed zero, raw nonfinite values, and full 32-bit ARGB.
Only organism fields `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the existing geometry allowance.
For finite geometry values, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Check geometric NaN classification and signed infinity explicitly.
No other tolerance or NaN substitution applies.
Immutable Java Color reference identity maps to exact ARGB value semantics.

## Setup and execution

Compile `tools/reference/SpecialOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.SpecialOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the isolated profile arguments recorded in provenance.
The helper rejects missing isolated profiles, escaping profile symlinks, and existing output directories before simulation access.
It creates its TSV with `CREATE_NEW`.
The existing runner bounds subprocesses and cleans their owned process groups.
The tested runtime is Java 21.0.12.1.
No GUI window, network operation, original-source edit, or global profile modification is required.

Each case resets source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive settings.
Initial organisms are zero, and initial oxygen is `1000`.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`, meta mutation is zero, and only GREEN has selectable weight seven.
The construction seed is `827364`.
Explicit `rng:seed` controls reset only the actual source Random before selected contacts.

The fixture overrides MOSQUITO cost to `0.125`, SPIKE to `0.25`, and OCHRE to `0.5`.
SILVER cost is `0.375`, EXPERIENCE `0.625`, BLUE `0.75`, DODGE `0.875`, and SKY `1`.
Individual cases explicitly override other settings where required.
These are labelled test inputs, not proposed balance changes.

Three real organisms are pasted and added through actual source methods.
The literal roles are `peer`, `victim`, and `killer`.
`peer` is the separate selected organism at `(1000,1000)`.
`victim` is the attacker at `(3500,3500)`.
`killer` is the contact recipient at `(2000,2000)`.
The separate selector avoids MainWindow callbacks.
Selection metadata remains an explicit source-only exclusion.

Five supplied genotype identities remain fixed as `g0..g4`.
`g0`, `g1`, and `g2` are explicit constructions.
`g3` is an actual clone of `g0`, or `g1` in the labelled cloned-peer case.
`g4` is an actual clone of `g0`.
A labelled case constructs both contact actors with the same `g0` object.
Input G/N blocks and construction recipes define all supplied genomes.
Post-call observations never become constructor inputs.

SPIKEPOINT actors receive ordinary SPIKE genes, then an explicit current SPIKEPOINT phenotype.
This selects the original endpoint-specific branch without claiming collision or endpoint eligibility checks occurred.
Actor and recipient traits, cached state, counters, and numerical controls remain explicit I inputs.
Nonfinite and inconsistent-cache cases use real placed objects with labelled internal scalar controls.
They do not establish public input validation or ordinary full-frame reachability.

## Canonical protocol

Rows reuse the [death-family observer protocol](death.README.md).
Each C row uses mode `canonical` and construction seed `827364`.
K rows contain stage, labelled operation, target `victim`, and `killer,segment,peer_segment`.
Operation labels are `touchEffects1.SPIKEPOINT`, `touchEffects1.OCHRE`, and `touchEffects1.SILVER`.
Actual selected indices appear in each command.
Most commands use attacker segment one and recipient segment zero.
Dedicated cases select attacker zero or recipient one.

Every actor view contains all 154 organism fields and three explicit genotype-reference holders.
Each snapshot contains ten world getter values, 52 statistics fields, and 49 public zero-argument getters.
Every genotype contains 28 fields, including reference identity and gene count.
Every gene contains all 40 source fields.
R records the following long, bounded integer, and raw double from a copied source Random.
The sorted inventory contains 104 exact typed control targets.

O `_world` and `_visibleWorld` remain named collaborator exclusions.
The selected source UI object remains named selection metadata.
No other fields or identities are skipped.
This protocol contains no V, tree, newborn D, or exception X rows.
These methods do not insert members or query spatial candidates.

Validation checks exact schemas, types, cardinalities, ordered genes, roles, references, command stages, and current attacker ARGB.
It also checks selected actual outcomes, unchanged genotypes, and applicable RNG invariants.
One validator assertion initially ignored the SILVER actor's supplied four prior kills.
Its failed script and receipt remain preserved.
Only that validator expectation changed; Java observations and comparison allowances did not change.

## Separate arithmetic diagnostic

Run `biogenesis.SpecialOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY diagnostic` with the same isolated profile arguments.
The helper catches only a reflected `ArithmeticException` from the original method.
The process exits with explicitly expected diagnostic status `20`.
It writes `special_contacts_invalid.tsv` privately, outside the canonical success corpus.
The provenance embeds its exact UTF-8 content and hash.

The actual SILVER attacker has one prior kill and enhancement.
The actual recipient has `-12` prior kills.
EXPERIENCE cost is `0.625`, with sufficient attacker energy and oxygen.
The source pays that cost before integer division encounters a wrapped zero denominator.
X records stage, exception class `java.lang.ArithmeticException`, and actual message `/ by zero`.
A clearly labelled `failed-step-0` snapshot records the actual partially changed state and RNG.
It is not a successful contact snapshot or clamped replacement output.
Two source runs and the JAR match the complete diagnostic bytes and exit status.
Public Rust exception translation remains a separate integration decision.

All six isolation guards pass.
All 74 original files retain their hashes, sizes, and modes.
All 30 prior TSV fixtures remain unchanged.
The Rust production file also retains its frozen hash.

These observations do not execute collision scheduling, complete frames, UI callbacks, networking, persistence, rendering, or player journeys.
They do not establish an exhaustive cross-product of contact predicates.
Rust replay and independent review remain separate evidence.
